_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Come, let us sing to the Lord, the great King above all gods.
We are his people, the sheep of his hand.
The Son of Man will come in glory and sit on his throne.
And he will know us by our mercy to the least.
God has seated Christ far above every rule and power.
He is head over all things for the church.
Come, let us worship Christ the King.
We bow before the Shepherd-King. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Lift your eyes to the throne at the end of all things, the Son of Man crowned in glory, the nations gathered before him like a shepherd dividing the flock.
Christ is King, and we are his.
Yet this King is the Shepherd who searches for the lost, binds up the broken, and carries the weak ones home.
Christ is King, and we are his.
He has been raised far above every ruler and power and given a name above every name, head over all things for us.
Christ is King, and we are his.
And he is known by this: a cup of water, a coat, a visit to the prison — as you did it to the least, you did it to the King.
Christ is King, and we are his.
So come, you sheep of his pasture, and bow before the Shepherd-King.
Christ is King, and we are his! Alleluia!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Come, sing to the Lord, the great King above all.
Christ is King, and we are his.
The Son of Man comes in glory to the throne.
Christ is King, and we are his.
This King is the Shepherd who seeks the lost.
Christ is King, and we are his.
Come, let us worship Christ the King.
We bow before the Shepherd-King. Amen.
